question.text: A 34-year-old man comes to the physician because of frequent headaches and blurry vision during the past 4 months. He has also had difficulties achieving an erection over the past few weeks. Physical examination shows a temporal visual field deficit bilaterally. An MRI of the brain shows an intrasellar mass. The mass is most likely derived from which of the following types of cells?

Given the options, the most likely cell type to be affected by a pituitary adenoma is lactotrophs, which are responsible for prolactin production. Prolactinomas are the most common type of pituitary adenoma and often present with these symptoms.

Thyrotrophs, somatotrophs, and gonadotrophs are less commonly associated with the specific constellation of symptoms described. Therefore, prolactinomas are the most likely diagnosis.
